Subject: SLA structure question — modular lanes + volume discounts

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo on Friday — the team was impressed with the routing and failover story. Procurement and engineering are aligned on wanting a smaller initial commitment, but with the option to expand into a multi-lane SLA as we scale. A couple of asks that would help us get to an internal PO: 

- Can you confirm whether uptime guarantees can be applied per-lane (e.g., 99.9% for production lane, 99.5% for non-prod), and how credits would be calculated in a mixed-lane account?
- Do you offer stepped discounts tied to committed monthly tokens or reserved capacity (we're starting smaller and want predictable step-up pricing)?
- We need an example workbook showing a blended price if we move 60% traffic to prod lane and 40% to standard lane.

Procurement also asked for a short list of what an escalation cadence looks like for the top lane (response SLA, 24/7 on-call, named TAM, escalation hours). Can you put something together we can present to legal & procurement?

Appreciate it —
Ellie Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

Hi Ellie,

Thanks — great questions. Looping in KarThik (pricing) and Ben (support packaging) to propose a compact, extensible structure and a sample workbook.

High level replies first:
- Yes, uptime guarantees can be lane-specific. Credits are assessed per-incident and applied proportionally to the impacted lane's committed resources; we can also offer an account-level blended credit in cases where an outage affects multiple lanes.
- We do stepped discounts tied to committed monthly token tiers and reserved capacity commits. Typical anchor points are 100M, 250M, 1B tokens/month — with larger step discounts and a Dedicated pool option for >1B.
- We'll prepare a blended pricing workbook and a short escalation cadence (on-call hours, named TAM, and contact tiers).

Ben/Karthik — can you produce: 1) a compact SLA matrix PDF we can attach to procurement, and 2) a sample blended-pricing sheet for 60/40 split? Also include one concession play (e.g., first-quarter price protection or onboarding credits) we can offer to keep initial commitment low.

I'll follow up with a short note we can present to Acme procurement/legal.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Ellie —

Taking a pass at numbers and the workbook. Key assumptions:
- Base list price (hosted API) = $0.00015 per token for generation tier (example).
- Production lane SLA (99.9%) has a 12% premium over base; Standard lane (99.5%) is +4%.
- Credit calculation model: per-incident token-value * incident-duration weight. If multiple lanes affected we do lane-weighted blended credit.

Attached: sla_modular_matrix_v1.pdf — concise table of lanes, guarantees, response windows, and the credit multipliers. Also attached a starter blended-pricing tab in the shared sheet (see link).

Concession play (to enable smaller initial commit):
- Offer: 3-month onboarding credit equal to 10% of committed monthly spend OR price protection (lock anchor price for first 6 months) — pick one.
- If they commit to 250M tokens/month within 90 days, we'll give a one-time implementation credit that amortizes across first invoice.

I'll convert the spreadsheet into a presentable example: 60% prod / 40% standard at 250M monthly committed tokens — gives effective blended price of $0.000138/token after lane premia and volume discount (see sheet).

Questions for procurement: do you need wording for "named TAM" and "escalation hours" in the Master Services Agreement (MSA), or would a separate Support Addendum suffice?

Team / Ellie — quick support packaging notes and a recommended escalation ladder: 

Summary (for procurement slide):
- Top lane (Production Premium): 99.9% uptime, 1-hour P1 response during business hours, 4-hour P1 response off-hours with 24/7 on-call for P0; named TAM included for commit >= 250M tokens/month.
- Mid lane (Standard): 99.5% uptime, 4-hour P1 response BH, 12-hour off-hours.
- Non-prod: 99.0%, business-hours response only.

Escalation cadence (example):
1) Triage (level 1): customer portal -> auto-ack within 15 mins;
2) Engineering triage (level 2): on-call engineer; 1 hour for prod P1;
3) Named TAM (level 3): 2 hours to engage and provide status to exec sponsor;
4) Exec Escalation: 4 hours to scheduled exec sync for impact > 6 hours or revenue-critical incidents.

Recommended concession to close: 1) 30% onboarding credit on first month (capped) OR 2) 3 months of price protection (no upward price movement) — whichever appears in the final PO. I prefer the price-protection approach as it keeps TAM/credits cleaner from an accounting perspective.

I'll draft a one-page Support Addendum with the ladder and contact matrix that legal can accept as an exhibit to the MSA.

-Ben
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference
